question: How do finite existence and coefficient behavior change when a positive correction power tends to zero?
motivation: The existing finite-ratio formula suggests a discontinuity at exactly zero power. Initial deterministic calculations were inspected before this validation plan; they are mathematical exploration,not registered empirical evidence.
claims_to_check: For a fixed predictor and sample,existence is nested as a strictly positive power decreases,under the stated full-rank condition
A sufficiently small positive power gives a finite root exactly when the unit-power recession function is strictly positive on nonzero human weak separators
The balanced oracle boundary has an explicit positive-power right limit exceeding the ordinary null threshold0.5
Finite roots can diverge as power tends to zero when the human MLE is unavailable

Gaussian_phase_validation.pairing: All powers and limiting feasibility use the same X,Y,Z draw;label budgets and proxy conditions are separate blocks
Gaussian_phase_validation.intercept: fixed zero;all feature coordinates independent standard Gaussian
Gaussian_phase_validation.zero_endpoint: ordinary separation/support check,never the vacuous zero interval LP
Gaussian_phase_validation.error0.5_role: uninformative oracle prediction;existence improvement must not be called information gain

independent_checks: Normal quadrature for the right-limit formula
Finite-power monotonicity with tolerance and no forced strict ordering after floating-point saturation
Original weighted-moment versus rescaled interval LP on120 draws
Analytic one-coordinate rescued,boundary and exterior examples
A two-coordinate coefficient path against a separately solved limiting linear program
